Auto-discovery idea: RNAPIISer2-P neighborhoods around polyA_RNA spots should survive cell-label negative controls¶

Rationale¶

Transcriptionally engaged nuclear regions should place mature RNA signal near elongating polymerase signal. A robustness hypothesis is that this proximity should disappear when cell identities are permuted.

Data used¶

Use 3D coordinates, cell IDs, polyA_RNA track values, and RNAPIISer2-P track values for all available cell types.

Analysis sketch¶

Select high polyA_RNA spots and high RNAPIISer2-P spots within each cell. The single parameter is the median nearest-neighbor distance from high polyA_RNA spots to high RNAPIISer2-P spots within the same cell.

Expected result¶

The observed nearest-neighbor distance should be smaller than distances obtained after permuting cell labels for RNAPIISer2-P spots.

Validation checks¶

Check required fields, enough cells and high-signal spots, finite distance output, a permutation p-value, deterministic seeded rerun, runtime, and a negative control using cell-label permutation.

Graphical abstract¶

Generated after notebook exploration with Pantheon file_manager.generate_image.

The code agent can freely add cells below this point.

Critique and compact analysis plan¶

This idea is testable with the available 3D spot coordinates, spot-level cell IDs, and IF track intensities. I will treat each chromatin spot as a candidate locus, select top-quartile polyA_RNA and RNAPIISer2-P spots within each cell, and compute per-cell nearest-neighbor distances from high-polyA spots to high-RNAPII spots. The explicit negative control will keep all RNAPIISer2-P coordinates and intensities intact but randomly permute RNAPIISer2-P cell labels, so any same-cell proximity should be lost if it depends on true cell identity. Because only 9 cells are available, the analysis is exploratory; the statistic is the median over per-cell medians, tested against a bounded seeded permutation null.

# Main compact exploration: top-quartile polyA_RNA to RNAPIISer2-P nearest-neighbor distance
# with a seeded cell-label permutation negative control.
import os
os.environ.setdefault('MPLBACKEND', 'Agg')
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg', force=True)
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import display, Image
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import json
from pathlib import Path

rng = np.random.default_rng(8675309)
result_path = RUN_OUTPUT_DIR / 'rnapiiser2-p-neighborhoods-around-polya-rna-spot-6bd867a3af_result.csv'
fig_path = RUN_OUTPUT_DIR / 'rnapiiser2-p-neighborhoods-around-polya-rna-spot-6bd867a3af_statistical_summary.png'
RUN_OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

coords = np.asarray(cdata.coords, dtype=float)
spots = cdata.spots.reset_index(drop=True).copy()
tracks = cdata.tracks.reset_index(drop=True)
spots['polyA_RNA'] = pd.to_numeric(tracks['polyA_RNA'], errors='coerce')
spots['RNAPIISer2_P'] = pd.to_numeric(tracks['RNAPIISer2-P'], errors='coerce')
spots[['x_um', 'y_um', 'z_um']] = coords
cell_type_map = cdata.cells['cell_type'].astype(str).to_dict()
spots['cell_type'] = spots['cell_id'].map(cell_type_map)

# Top quartile is computed within each cell. To keep pairwise distance work bounded,
# sample at most this many high spots per marker per cell after thresholding.
max_high_spots_per_cell = 400
cell_ids = sorted(spots['cell_id'].dropna().astype(str).unique())
selected_polyA = {}
selected_rnap = {}
cell_rows = []

def _sample_indices(indices, max_n):
    indices = np.asarray(indices, dtype=int)
    if len(indices) > max_n:
        return np.sort(rng.choice(indices, size=max_n, replace=False))
    return np.sort(indices)

def _nn_median(poly_coords, rnap_coords):
    if len(poly_coords) == 0 or len(rnap_coords) == 0:
        return np.nan
    # Chunk polyA queries to avoid a large all-vs-all allocation.
    mins = []
    chunk = 200
    for start in range(0, len(poly_coords), chunk):
        p = poly_coords[start:start+chunk]
        d2 = ((p[:, None, :] - rnap_coords[None, :, :]) ** 2).sum(axis=2)
        mins.append(np.sqrt(d2.min(axis=1)))
    return float(np.median(np.concatenate(mins)))

for cid in cell_ids:
    mask = (spots['cell_id'].astype(str).values == cid)
    idx = np.flatnonzero(mask)
    sub = spots.iloc[idx]
    poly_q75 = float(np.nanquantile(sub['polyA_RNA'], 0.75))
    rnap_q75 = float(np.nanquantile(sub['RNAPIISer2_P'], 0.75))
    poly_idx_all = idx[np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(sub['polyA_RNA'].values) & (sub['polyA_RNA'].values >= poly_q75))]
    rnap_idx_all = idx[np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(sub['RNAPIISer2_P'].values) & (sub['RNAPIISer2_P'].values >= rnap_q75))]
    poly_idx = _sample_indices(poly_idx_all, max_high_spots_per_cell)
    rnap_idx = _sample_indices(rnap_idx_all, max_high_spots_per_cell)
    selected_polyA[cid] = poly_idx
    selected_rnap[cid] = rnap_idx
    med_nn = _nn_median(coords[poly_idx], coords[rnap_idx])
    cell_rows.append({
        'cell_id': cid,
        'cell_type': str(cell_type_map.get(cid, 'unknown')),
        'n_polyA_high_all': int(len(poly_idx_all)),
        'n_RNAPIISer2P_high_all': int(len(rnap_idx_all)),
        'n_polyA_high_sampled': int(len(poly_idx)),
        'n_RNAPIISer2P_high_sampled': int(len(rnap_idx)),
        'polyA_q75': poly_q75,
        'RNAPIISer2P_q75': rnap_q75,
        'median_polyA_to_RNAPIISer2P_nn_um': med_nn,
    })

per_cell = pd.DataFrame(cell_rows)
valid_cell_medians = per_cell['median_polyA_to_RNAPIISer2P_nn_um'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).dropna().values
observed_statistic = float(np.median(valid_cell_medians)) if len(valid_cell_medians) else np.nan

# Permutation null: pool the sampled high RNAPIISer2-P spots and shuffle their cell labels while
# preserving the number of RNAPII spots assigned to each cell. polyA cell labels remain fixed.
rnap_pool = np.concatenate([selected_rnap[cid] for cid in cell_ids if len(selected_rnap[cid])])
rnap_counts = {cid: len(selected_rnap[cid]) for cid in cell_ids}
n_permutations = 500
null_stats = []
if len(valid_cell_medians) >= 2 and len(rnap_pool) > 0 and all(len(selected_polyA[cid]) > 0 for cid in cell_ids):
    for _ in range(n_permutations):
        shuffled_pool = rng.permutation(rnap_pool)
        cursor = 0
        perm_meds = []
        for cid in cell_ids:
            n_r = rnap_counts[cid]
            assigned_rnap = shuffled_pool[cursor:cursor+n_r]
            cursor += n_r
            if n_r > 0 and len(selected_polyA[cid]) > 0:
                perm_meds.append(_nn_median(coords[selected_polyA[cid]], coords[assigned_rnap]))
        perm_meds = np.asarray(perm_meds, dtype=float)
        perm_meds = perm_meds[np.isfinite(perm_meds)]
        if len(perm_meds):
            null_stats.append(float(np.median(perm_meds)))
null_stats = np.asarray(null_stats, dtype=float)

if len(null_stats) >= 100 and np.isfinite(observed_statistic):
    # One-sided test: observed proximity is smaller than permuted-cell null.
    p_value = float((1 + np.sum(null_stats <= observed_statistic)) / (len(null_stats) + 1))
    null_median = float(np.median(null_stats))
    effect_size = float(null_median - observed_statistic)  # positive means observed is closer than null
    hypothesis_test_status = 'pass'
    test_note = 'Seeded one-sided cell-label permutation test completed.'
else:
    p_value = 1.0
    null_median = float(np.nanmedian(null_stats)) if len(null_stats) else np.nan
    effect_size = float(null_median - observed_statistic) if np.isfinite(null_median) and np.isfinite(observed_statistic) else 0.0
    hypothesis_test_status = 'insufficient_data'
    test_note = 'Too few finite cell medians or permutation draws for a formal test.'

test_method = f'one-sided cell-label permutation test ({len(null_stats)} permutations)'
null_hypothesis = 'The median same-cell nearest-neighbor distance from high polyA_RNA spots to high RNAPIISer2-P spots is no smaller than under permuted RNAPIISer2-P cell labels.'
alternative_hypothesis = 'The observed median same-cell nearest-neighbor distance is smaller than the cell-label-permuted null distribution.'

# Add required test columns to every result row and write the compact table.
result_table = per_cell.copy()
result_table['observed_statistic_um'] = observed_statistic
result_table['null_median_um'] = null_median
result_table['effect_size_um_null_minus_observed'] = effect_size
result_table['p_value'] = p_value
result_table['test_method'] = test_method
result_table['hypothesis_test_status'] = hypothesis_test_status
result_table.to_csv(result_path, index=False)

analysis_summary = {
    'idea_id': IDEA.idea_id,
    'parameter_name': 'polyA_to_RNAPIISer2P_nn_um',
    'parameter_value': observed_statistic,
    'observed_statistic': observed_statistic,
    'effect_size': effect_size,
    'p_value': p_value,
    'test_method': test_method,
    'null_hypothesis': null_hypothesis,
    'alternative_hypothesis': alternative_hypothesis,
    'hypothesis_test_status': hypothesis_test_status,
    'n_selected_cells': int(result_table['cell_id'].nunique()),
    'n_rows': int(len(result_table)),
    'n_polyA_high_sampled_total': int(result_table['n_polyA_high_sampled'].sum()),
    'n_RNAPIISer2P_high_sampled_total': int(result_table['n_RNAPIISer2P_high_sampled'].sum()),
    'n_permutations_requested': int(n_permutations),
    'n_null_permutations_finite': int(len(null_stats)),
    'max_high_spots_per_cell': int(max_high_spots_per_cell),
    'negative_control': 'RNAPIISer2-P high-spot cell labels were permuted across cells while preserving per-cell RNAPII counts.',
    'result_path': str(result_path),
    'figure_path': str(fig_path),
    'notes': [test_note, 'Top-quartile thresholds were computed within each cell; selected high spots were capped per marker/cell for bounded runtime.'],
}

# Statistical figure: null distribution with observed statistic, plus per-cell observed medians.
plt.rcParams.update({'figure.facecolor': 'white', 'axes.facecolor': 'white', 'font.size': 10})
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.2), constrained_layout=True)
ax = axes[0]
if len(null_stats):
    ax.hist(null_stats, bins=25, color='#bdbdbd', edgecolor='white', label='Permuted RNAPIISer2-P cell labels')
ax.axvline(observed_statistic, color='#b2182b', linewidth=2.5, label='Observed')
ax.axvline(null_median, color='#2166ac', linewidth=2, linestyle='--', label='Null median')
ax.set_xlabel('Median per-cell nearest-neighbor distance (µm)')
ax.set_ylabel('Permutation count')
ax.set_title('Hypothesis-test evidence')
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
ax.text(0.03, 0.97, f'p = {p_value:.4f}\neffect = {effect_size:.3f} µm\nn = {len(result_table)} cells\n{test_method}',
        transform=ax.transAxes, va='top', ha='left', fontsize=8,
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white', edgecolor='#cccccc', alpha=0.9))

ax2 = axes[1]
order = result_table.sort_values(['cell_type', 'cell_id']).reset_index(drop=True)
colors = {'Granule': '#1b9e77', 'Bergmann': '#d95f02', 'Purkinje': '#7570b3'}
bar_colors = [colors.get(ct, '#666666') for ct in order['cell_type']]
ax2.bar(np.arange(len(order)), order['median_polyA_to_RNAPIISer2P_nn_um'], color=bar_colors, edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.4)
ax2.axhline(observed_statistic, color='#b2182b', linestyle='-', linewidth=1.5, label='Observed median')
ax2.axhline(null_median, color='#2166ac', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, label='Null median')
ax2.set_xticks(np.arange(len(order)))
ax2.set_xticklabels(order['cell_type'] + '\n' + order['cell_id'].astype(str), rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=7)
ax2.set_ylabel('Nearest-neighbor distance (µm)')
ax2.set_title('Per-cell high polyA → high RNAPIISer2-P')
ax2.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
for spine_ax in axes:
    spine_ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    spine_ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
fig.suptitle('High polyA_RNA spots are compared with high RNAPIISer2-P neighborhoods', fontsize=12)
fig.savefig(fig_path, dpi=200, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()
display(Image(filename=str(fig_path)))

display(result_table)
print(json.dumps(analysis_summary, indent=2))

checks = {check: 'not_run' for check in IDEA.validation_checks}

def _check_keys(prefix):
    return [key for key in checks if key == prefix or key.startswith(prefix + ':')]

def _set_check(prefix, value):
    keys = _check_keys(prefix)
    if not keys:
        checks[prefix] = value
        return
    for key in keys:
        checks[key] = value

def _check_status(prefix):
    values = [checks[key] for key in _check_keys(prefix)]
    if not values:
        return None
    if 'fail' in values:
        return 'fail'
    if all(value == 'pass' for value in values):
        return 'pass'
    return values[0]

Final interpretation¶

Hypothesis. High polyA_RNA chromatin-associated spots are spatially closer to high RNAPIISer2-P spots within the same cell than expected under a cell-label permutation negative control.

Exploration. The notebook operationalized the idea as polyA_to_RNAPIISer2P_nn_um: median same-cell nearest-neighbor 3D distance from top-quartile polyA_RNA spots to top-quartile RNAPIISer2-P spots. using modalities chromatin_tracing, if_tracks, cell_metadata in cell type(s) Granule, Bergmann, Purkinje. Required data fields checked: coords, spots.cell_id, tracks.polyA_RNA, tracks.RNAPIISer2-P, cells.cell_type.

Statistical evidence. U-Chrom runner status: Notebook verified. Test: one-sided cell-label permutation test (500 permutations). Observed statistic: 0.3206; effect size: 0.391; parameter value: 0.3206; p-value: 0.001996.

Conclusion. Contradicted (Opposite direction). The hypothesis test is significant, but the observed effect is in the opposite direction from the idea.

What verification means. Notebook verified means the run passed schema/data checks, produced finite numeric output, and included an explicit p-value/effect-size hypothesis test. It does not mean the biological hypothesis is automatically correct.

Checks passed. deterministic_rerun, finite_numeric_output, minimum_cell_count, minimum_spot_or_trace_count, negative_control_or_permutation, required_fields_exist, runtime_under_budget, statistical_hypothesis_test.

Main caveat. Seeded one-sided cell-label permutation test completed.

Final interpretation¶

The scaffold was completed with a lightweight inspection cell and a main statistical exploration. Required fields were present, coordinates were finite, and the analysis selected top-quartile polyA_RNA and RNAPIISer2-P spots within each of the 9 cells, capped at 400 high spots per marker/cell for bounded runtime.

Hypothesis test. The observed median per-cell nearest-neighbor distance from high polyA_RNA spots to high RNAPIISer2-P spots was 0.3206 µm. A seeded one-sided RNAPIISer2-P cell-label permutation test with 500 finite permutations gave p = 0.001996 and effect size = 0.3910 µm (null median minus observed), supporting shorter same-cell neighborhoods than the permuted control.

Visual QA. The saved statistical figure is non-blank and readable: it shows the permutation null distribution with observed and null-median reference lines, plus a per-cell bar comparison with axes in µm and annotated p-value/effect size/sample size/test method. No misleading decoration was apparent.
